stem: On a live service, which keys appear in the dictionary `session.details()` returns? (Select all that apply.)

explanation.correct: `Session.details()` describes the session itself, not its jobs: `state` (open / active / inactive / closed), `accepting_jobs`, `max_time` (the maximum session length allowed by your plan), the lifecycle timestamps `last_job_started` / `last_job_completed` / `started_at` / `closed_at` / `activated_at`, plus `id`, `backend_name`, `interactive_timeout`, `active_timeout`, `mode` and `usage_time`. Note that the dictionary comes from the server: in local testing mode (a Session built on a fake backend) `details()` returns `None`, because there is no server-side session to describe.

distractors.B: A queue position belongs to an individual job (the Workloads view), not to the session description; the 0.48 `details()` builds a fixed 14-key dict and `queue_position` is not among them.
distractors.F: Results belong to individual jobs (`job.result()`); a session never carries result data.
